question: A synovial fluid white cell count of 20,000 cells/mm³ with 85% neutrophils is diagnostic of septic arthritis and mandates immediate antibiotic therapy and joint drainage.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. The threshold for presumptive septic arthritis is WCC > 50,000 cells/mm³. A count of 20,000 with neutrophilia falls in the 'inflammatory' range, which includes crystal arthropathies and reactive arthritis. Do not automatically equate neutrophilic synovial fluid with infection — send cultures and interpret in clinical context.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. While 20,000 cells/mm³ with neutrophil predominance is consistent with an inflammatory arthritis, the generally accepted threshold for presumptive septic arthritis is WCC > 50,000 cells/mm³ (some authorities use >50,000 with >90% PMNs). At 20,000, crystal arthropathy (gout, pseudogout) or reactive arthritis must be actively excluded. Culture result and clinical context are essential before committing to septic arthritis treatment.
